submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Fe 0.84, Sb 0.16) had the highest measured EQE, 0.0178%. Hematite is stable according to MACE and absorbs 2.1 eV light. EQE fell steeply as Sb increased: 0.0032% at index 4 and 0.0015% at index 13.

rejected.reason: Near FeSbO4. MEGNet predicts a gap of about 2.08 eV, but the measured EQE was only 0.0015%.
Fe2O3+FeSbO4 mixed region. EQE was 0.0032%, about 5x lower than index 0.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gap of rutile FeSbO4 (2.08 eV) is just below the 2.1 eV photon energy so it should absorb; index 13 (Fe 0.52) is closest to FeSbO4 stoichiometry. Fe2O3 predicted 2.77 eV (HSE overestimates; real ~2.1) — Fe-rich end is the alternative.

Support: MACE places Fe2O3 (hematite) on the hull (0 eV/atom). So the Fe-rich film at index 0 should be mostly Sb-doped hematite, a known photoanode that absorbs 2.1 eV light. The near-FeSbO4 point gave only 0.0015% EQE.

Mildly supportive. MACE puts FeSbO4 essentially on the hull (0.0016 eV/atom), so films between the two ends should be a two-phase Fe2O3 + FeSbO4 mix. At index 4 hematite still dominates, and the FeSbO4 interface may help separate charge. This is the GP's high-mean/high-uncertainty option. Against it: the measured trend so far (0.018 at index 0 vs 0.0015 at index 13) favors more Fe.
